LIBERMAN BACKS EISENKOT, RULES OUT COALITION WITH NETANYAHU Israeli opposition leader Avigdor Liberman reportedly said his party will recommend Gadi Eisenkot to lead the next government. Liberman reiterated that Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office, ruling out joining a coalition with him even under a rotating premiership. He also said Yair Lapid wants to become Speaker of the Knesset and pledged support for his candidacy.

MIZUHO REITERATES $165 TARGET ON STRATEGY ($MSTR ) Mizuho maintained its Outperform rating and $165 price target on Strategy following its Q3 2026 earnings call. Analyst Dan Dolev highlighted a stronger balance sheet, with 848,517 BTC held, net leverage falling to 2.4% from 8.4%, and $5.1 billion in USD assets covering 3.4 years of dividends and interest. However, Bitcoin per share has declined 3.7% year to date, raising dilution concerns.

MUSK THROTTLES GROK BOT AS AI COSTS BECOME UNSUSTAINABLE Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX intentionally restricted Grok Bot usage over Halloween weekend, citing operating costs that were “unsustainably high relative to revenue.” Some users reported their weekly usage jumping from 50% to 100% without additional activity. The restrictions come despite SpaceX reporting that AI accounts for 52% of company income, with its Super Intelligence division generating $431 million in profit.

POWER OUTAGE HITS DOWNTOWN WASHINGTON AHEAD OF ELECTION DAY More than 1,100 customers lost power in Washington, D.C., just blocks from the White House, on the eve of the US midterm elections. Utility provider Pepco reports 1,176 affected customers, with a substation failure identified as the probable cause. Outages are concentrated in Foggy Bottom, home to the State Department.

IRAN REJECTS US APPROACH AS “UNACCEPTABLE” Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson criticized Washington's approach, saying Tehran will not accept being treated with a “top-down attitude.” The spokesperson emphasized sovereign equality and national self-determination, accusing the US of violating international principles in its dealings with Cuba, Venezuela and Palestine. The comments come amid reports of potential progress in US–Iran diplomatic talks.

US MIDTERMS HISTORICALLY SIGNAL STRONG STOCK MARKET GAINS The S&P 500 has gained an average of approximately 7% during the fourth quarter of midterm election years, according to Deutsche Bank strategist Parag Thatte. Over the past 23 midterm election years, the index posted fourth-quarter gains in 21, an impressive 91% historical success rate.

US FACTORY ORDERS SURGE 1.8%, BEATING EXPECTATIONS US factory orders rose 1.8% in September, exceeding the 1.2% consensus forecast and accelerating from August's upwardly revised 0.3% gain. Orders excluding transportation increased 1.3%, while orders excluding defense jumped 2.0%, signaling broad-based manufacturing strength. Durable goods orders were revised higher to +1.9%, and core capital goods orders improved to +0.6%, with shipments rising 1.2%.

US JOB OPENINGS RISE TO 7.52 MILLION IN SEPTEMBER US job openings increased to 7.523 million in September, up from an upwardly revised 7.190 million in August, signaling stronger labor demand. Hiring rose to 5.402 million, while voluntary quits climbed to 3.365 million, pushing the quits rate to 2.1% from 1.9%. Meanwhile, layoffs declined to 1.641 million from 1.768 million, with the layoff rate falling to 1.0%.
